title: 这, 那 and measure words
explain: 这 means this and 那 means that. Before a noun they need a measure word: 这个人 (this person), 那本书 (that book). 这个 and 那个 can also stand alone: 我喜欢这个。 Plurals are 这些 and 那些. Places are 这儿 / 这里 (here) and 那儿 / 那里 (there).
Chinese counts with a measure word between the number and the noun: 三个苹果, 两本书. The all-purpose one is 个.

Some nouns want a specific one: 本 for books, 件 for clothes (and for matters), 只 (zhī) for small animals, 口 for people in a family, 家 for shops and companies, 块 or 元 for money, and 杯 for cups of drinks.
Ask how many with 几 + measure word: 你有几本书？

examples.en: I want to buy a new piece of clothing.
There are four people in my family.
I would like a cup of tea.

mistakes: Use the right measure word: 三本书, not 三个书. Use 个 only when no special one fits.

q.en: I want to buy a new piece of clothing.
q.explain: Number + 件 + clothing.
本 is the measure word for books.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I have a cat?
q.explain: Small animals take 只.

q.en: There are three people in his family.
q.explain: 口 counts the members of a family.

q.en: How many books do you have?
q.explain: 几 + measure word asks how many.

title: Numbers, 两, money, age and 第
explain: 一 二 三 四 五 六 七 八 九 十. Then 十一 (11), 二十 (20), 二十一 (21). 一百 is 100 and 一百零五 is 105 (零 fills the gap). 一千 is 1,000.
There are two words for two: 二 for counting, numbers and dates (二十, 二月), and 两 before a measure word (两个, 两本书).
半 means half: 一半 (half of it). Money uses 块 (spoken) or 元 (written), often with 钱: 三块钱, 三十元. One and a half yuan is 一块半.
第 makes an ordinal number: 第一天 means 'the first day'.
Age uses 岁 and needs no 是: 我八岁。

examples.en: This bun is one and a half yuan.

examples.zh: 今天是我学汉语的第一天。
examples.en: Today is my first day of learning Chinese.

mistakes: Say 两个人, not 二个人. But 二 is right in numbers and dates: 二十, 二月二号.

q.en: This bun is one and a half yuan.
q.explain: 块 + 半 means one and a half yuan.
Before a measure word, two is 两.
岁 is used for age. There is no 是.

q.zh: 今天是我学汉语的第一天。
q.en: Today is my first day of learning Chinese.
q.explain: 第 makes ordinal numbers.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I want to buy two apples?
q.en: I want to buy two apples.
q.explain: Use 两 before a measure word.

title: Time, dates and days
explain: Clock time is number + 点 (o'clock), then + 分 (minutes) or 半 (half): 七点, 八点零五分, 七点半. Say 两点 for 2 o'clock.
Dates go from big to small: year, month, day. Say 月 and 号 (spoken) or 日 (written): 十月三十号. Weekdays are 星期 + number: 星期一 to 星期六. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日. Ask with 几: 今天星期几？ 现在几点？

A point in time goes before the verb, either right after the subject or at the start of the sentence: 我七点起床 or 七点我起床. Not after the verb. (How long something lasted is different and comes after the verb: 我住了三天.)
A time or date does not need a verb: 现在七点半。 With 是 it also works: 现在是八点零五分。

examples.en: I get up at seven o'clock.
What day of the week is it today?
I am at home on Sunday.

mistakes: Say 两点 for 2 o'clock, not 二点.
A point in time goes before the verb: 我七点起床, not 我起床七点.

q.en: I get up at seven o'clock.
q.explain: The time comes before the verb.
几点 asks for the hour.

q.en: What day of the week is it today?
q.explain: 星期 + 几 asks the weekday.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: It is 2 o'clock?
q.explain: Use 两点 for 2 o'clock.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Today is October 30th?
q.explain: Dates go from big to small: month, then day.

title: 在: where something happens
explain: 在 means 'at / in'. 在 + place usually goes before the verb: 我在家吃饭 means 'I eat at home'. (A few verbs take it after, like 住在学校 'live at school'.)
在 can also be a verb, 'to be at': 我在家。他不在学校。
Ask where with 在哪儿 or 在哪里: 你在哪儿工作？
mistakes: The place goes before the verb: 我在家吃饭, not 我吃饭在家.

q.explain: 在 + place comes before the verb.
在 means 'at'.
哪儿 asks where.
不 goes before 在.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I study at school?
q.explain: The place comes before the verb.

title: Positions and where things are
explain: 上 (on) and 里 (inside) go right after the noun: 桌子上, 房间里. For under, outside, in front and behind, add 边 (side): 桌子下边, 房间外边, 学校前边, 学校后边. 这边 and 那边 work the same way.
Thing + 在 + place says where the thing is: 书在桌子上。
Place + 有 + thing says what is there: 桌子上有一本书。
Place + 是 + thing identifies what is there: 我家外边是一家商店 (What is outside my home is a shop). 有 only says that something exists there.

examples.en: The book is on the table.
There is water in the cup.
There is a book on the table.
Outside my home there is a shop.

mistakes: Do not use 在 for 'there is': 桌子上有一本书, not 桌子上在一本书.

q.en: There is water in the cup.
q.explain: Place + 有 + thing.

q.en: The book is on the table.
q.explain: 上 goes after the noun.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: There is a book on the table?
q.en: There is a book on the table.
q.explain: 'There is' uses 有.

q.en: Outside my home there is a shop.
q.explain: Place + 是 + thing names what is there.
Thing + 在 + place.

title: 想 and 要: wanting and offering
explain: 想 + verb means 'want to' or 'would like to': 我想喝茶。 It is soft and polite, so it is the word to use when you offer or ask what someone wants: 你想喝茶吗？ (Would you like some tea?) 你想吃什么？ (What would you like to eat?)
要 also means 'want', but it is more direct. It works with a noun, which is how you order or buy: 我要一个包子。 With a verb: 我要休息。
A plain verb question is not an offer. 你喝茶吗？ means 'Do you drink tea?' and asks about a habit. To ask 'Would you like tea?', add 想: 你想喝茶吗？
The negative of 想 is 不想: 我不想吃。 不要 is 'don't!' or a firm refusal.

examples.en: I want to go to China.
What would you like to drink?
I don't want anything to eat.

mistakes: 你喝茶吗？ is not an offer. It asks whether you drink tea. Offer with 你想喝茶吗？
不想 is 'do not want to'. 不要 is 'don't!'

q.explain: 想 turns the question into an offer.

q.prompt: Which sentence offers someone tea: 'Would you like some tea?'
q.explain: 你喝茶吗？ asks whether you drink tea. 想 makes it an offer.

q.en: What would you like to drink?
q.explain: 想 + verb asks what someone would like.
要 + noun is how you order.

q.en: I don't want anything to eat.
q.explain: 不 goes in front of 想.

title: 会, 能, 可以: can
explain: 会: you know how to, a skill you learned. 我会做饭。你会开车吗？
能: you are able to, or the situation allows it. 我明天能来。你能来吗？
可以: you are allowed to. It is how you ask for permission: 我可以坐这儿吗？ To say yes, answer 可以.
They overlap: 能 is also used to ask permission. The negatives are 不会 (don't know how), 不能 (can't) and 不可以 (not allowed).

examples.en: I can speak a little Chinese.

mistakes: Do not use 会 to ask permission: 我可以坐这儿吗？, not 我会坐这儿吗？

q.explain: 可以 asks for permission.
会 is for skills you learned.
能 is for being able to, because the situation allows it.

q.prompt: Which sentence asks: Can you speak Chinese? (a skill)
q.explain: 会 is for a learned skill. 可以 would ask whether you are allowed to.
可以 is for permission.

title: 都, 也, 还, 再 and joining sentences
explain: These adverbs go after the subject and before the verb or adjective: 我们都是学生。我也是学生。
都 means all or both: 我们都很好。 With 不, it means none of us: 我们都不喝茶。
也 means also or too. It goes before 不: 我也不是学生 means 'I am not a student either'. 我也是 means 'Me too'. Do not put 也 at the end of a sentence.
还 means also, else or still: 你还想吃什么？ (What else would you like to eat?)
再 means again, for something that has not happened yet: 明天再来。
Two short sentences can sit side by side with a comma and no 'and': 爸爸是老师，妈妈也是老师。

examples.en: What else would you like to eat?

examples.zh: 爸爸是老师，妈妈也是老师。
examples.en: Dad is a teacher, and Mom is a teacher too.

mistakes: 也 goes before the verb: 我也喜欢茶, not 我喜欢茶也.
都 goes after the subject: 他们都在学校, not 都他们在学校.

q.zh: 爸爸是老师，妈妈也是老师。
q.en: Dad is a teacher, and Mom is a teacher too.
q.explain: 也 goes before the second 是.
也 goes before the verb.
都 goes after the subject.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I like tea too?
q.explain: 也 comes before the verb, never at the end.

q.en: What else would you like to eat?
q.explain: 还 means 'else' here.

title: A-not-A questions
explain: Another way to ask a yes/no question: say the verb, then 不, then the verb again. 你是不是老师？ 你去不去学校？ (Are you going to school or not?)
For 有, use 没: 你有没有手机？
Do not add 吗 to an A-not-A question.
With two-syllable verbs the first verb is often shortened in speech: 你喜欢不喜欢茶？ can also be 你喜不喜欢茶？, and 你认识不认识他？ can be 你认不认识他？ Both are fine.
mistakes: No 吗 here: 你去不去？, not 你去不去吗？

q.explain: Verb + 不 + verb.
不 sits between the two verbs.

q.prompt: Which sentence asks: Do you have a phone?
q.explain: 有 uses 没: 有没有.
The A-not-A form already makes the question.
是不是 goes in the middle.
